blog_news.title: South Korea’s power giant KEPCO confirms data breach impacting 1.5 million
blog_news.description: A threat actor breached the internal network of Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO) and accessed two systems containing customer, employee, and contractor data. [...]

blog_news.title: OpenRouter drops AI providers over leaked prompts and secrets
blog_news.description: OpenRouter removed three AI providers from its platform after discovering that they had violated their stated data-handling policies and exposed sensitive data. [...]

blog_news.title: Microsoft Azure flaw exploited to steal customers' API credentials
blog_news.description: Microsoft is warning customers that a security vulnerability in Azure API Management (APIM) Classic tiers was exploited to steal stored API credentials, with Norwegian authorities linking the flaw to cyberattacks against energy companies. [...]

blog_news.title: Spanish LaLiga confirms hackers stole soccer fans’ personal data
blog_news.description: LaLiga, Spain's top men's football league, disclosed a data breach that exposed personal information belonging to users of its services and those of some affiliated clubs. [...]

blog_news.title: GlobeTopper loses $2.5 million after hackers steal $70k in gift cards
blog_news.description: A cyberattack disrupted operations at B2B top-up solutions provider GlobeTopper, causing an estimated $2.5 million in lost revenue, while the attacker redeemed digital gift cards worth $70,000. [...]

blog_news.title: AI Agents Are Creating a Shared Responsibility Gap
blog_news.description: AI agents operate across multiple platforms, creating security gaps when no single vendor can see or control their actions. Token Security examines the shared responsibility problem and explains how organizations can better manage agent identities, permissions, and accountability. [...]

blog_news.title: Microsoft testing fix for Windows 11 Bluetooth audio quality drops
blog_news.description: Microsoft is working to fix a long-standing Windows issue that has been causing significant audio quality drops for Bluetooth headphone users. [...]

blog_news.title: Call center operator gets 8 years for helping scam 30,000 Americans
blog_news.description: A Peruvian call center operator was sentenced to eight years in prison for helping steal millions of dollars from over 30,000 Spanish-speaking US residents in a years-long government-impersonation fraud scheme. [...]

blog_news.title: OpenAI and Cisco Unveil AI-Assisted Linux Security Tool to Block Exploits Before Patching
blog_news.description:
OpenAI and Cisco have teamed up to launch Shirudo (meaning "shield" in Japanese), an open-source Linux runtime that allows artificial intelligence (AI) agents to defend systems without downtime.

"It lets agents write dynamic eBPF controls to shield systems from exploits, giving defenders more time to test and roll out patches," OpenAI said in a post on X.

blog_news.description:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Monday added two flaws impacting N-able MailAssure and MONAI Label to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation.

The critical vulnerabilities are listed below -


  CVE-2026-134624 (CVSS score: 9.3) - A server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in N-able MailAssure's LDAP

blog_news.title: Webworm Suspected of Modifying SoftEther VPN to Evade Detection and Hide Remote Access
blog_news.description:
The China-aligned threat actor known as Webworm is suspected to be using a custom version of the open-source SoftEther VPN Bridge tool in an attempt to remove recognizable detection fingerprints, while disguising it as network-monitoring software to establish covert remote access to compromised networks.

The modified variant "implements various tricks to hide itself from security tools,"

blog_news.description:
A stolen key. A trusted message. A routine update. None of these looks like the start of a major security problem. That's partly why they work. Attackers don't always need to break down a door. Sometimes they just use one that's already open.

blog_news.title: Critical binary-parser Flaw Enables JavaScript Injection via Malicious Parser Definitions
blog_news.description:
A critical security flaw has been disclosed in the popular binary-parser library that could allow an attacker who controls parser definitions to execute arbitrary code.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-134814 (CVSS score: 9.2 / 8.1), is a case of code injection impacting binary-parser versions prior to 2.3.1.

"Binary-parser before 2.3.1 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows

blog_news.title: Hackers Exploit Critical ScreenConnect Flaw to Hijack MSP Technician PCs Without Warning
blog_news.description:
Threat actors are exploiting a now-patched security flaw in ConnectWise ScreenConnect to target managed service provider (MSP) servers.

The activity revolves around CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS score: 9.9), a critical ScreenConnect client flaw that allows a guest to transfer and execute a malicious payload on a connecting technician's host.

"On November 12, 2026, we observed one managed service

blog_news.title: N-able Discloses Critical Mail Assure Vulnerability Found During Breach Investigation
blog_news.description:
N-able yesterday disclosed a critical flaw it found while investigating the breach of its Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud, an email filtering service it runs for managed service providers.

The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-134624, is a server-side request forgery (SSRF) flaw. It allowed a user with high-level API access to open connections to internal systems of the user's choosing on the

blog_news.title: Hackers Exploit Critical ASP.NET Anti-CSRF Library Flaw Allowing Unauthenticated RCE
blog_news.description:
Cybersecurity researchers have urged users to discontinue using a legacy ASP.NET anti-CSRF library named Idunno.AntiCsrf ("Idunno.AntiCsrf.dll") following the discovery of a critical vulnerability that has been exploited in the wild.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-131914, carries a CVSS score of 9.3 out of 10.0. The issue affects versions 0.9.1.0 and 0.9.1 Beta, and relates to an

blog_news.title: CTO of ‘RansomwareHelp’ Indicted for Wire Fraud
blog_news.description: The chief technology officer and co-founder of ransomwarehelp.com, a six year old Florida business that claimed to use "advanced cryptographic tools" to restore data locked by ransomware, has been charged with wire fraud after an FBI sting operation found the company was simply paying the attackers for a decryption key and charging victims a markup for work that was never performed.

blog_news.title: Attackers Used Optimizely to A/B Test Malware on Top Websites
blog_news.description: At least 178 top web destinations unwittingly served a variety of malware exploits against visitors over the past 24 hours thanks to a security vulnerability involving Optimizely, a company that helps websites customize user experiences and test out new features. Experts say the incident, which saw data-stealing malicious software silently injected into sites like the BBC, CNN, Equifax, Ledger and Zoom, was exacerbated by the reality that few popular websites enforce strict rules on the sources of third-party content.

blog_news.title: Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?
blog_news.description: The cybercrime group Qilin has emerged as the world's most active ransomware affiliate program, claiming at least 365 victim organizations in the past three months alone. But even top Russian hackers make operational security mistakes, and the administrator of Qilin has made a few key missteps over the last decade that all point to a 36-year-old man living in St. Petersburg, Russia.

blog_news.title: Microsoft Fixes Nearly 1,100 Security Vulnerabilities
blog_news.description: Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month's Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws -- including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook -- and comes amid important security updates from other software makers, including Adobe, Apple, Google and Mozilla.

blog_news.title: Want to Rent an Internet Address at the White House?
blog_news.description: Several staffers at the White House are using computers or mobile devices equipped with residential proxy services that render their internet address available for others to rent, security experts warned today. One of the proxy services is a Russian company whose founder's web hosting business was ground zero for cyberattacks against election systems in Arizona and Illinois in 2016.

blog_news.title: Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies
blog_news.description: Google said today it worked with industry partners to dismantle a botnet made up of more than 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes that ship with malicious software which secretly rents the user's Internet connection out to strangers and conducts advertising fraud. Experts involved in the takedown say the action is likely to sever the botnet's access to more than 10 million additional compromised systems, including other Internet of Things (IoT) products such as Android-based healthcare devices and karaoke machines.

blog_news.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
blog_news.description: Expect to see quite a few websites serving "404" or "Page Not Found" errors today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild.

blog_news.title: Feds Suspect Ransom Negotiator Ran ShinyHunters Extortion Site
blog_news.description: U.S. federal investigators pursuing the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently stole highly sensitive data from the FBI have identified executives at two different ransomware negotiation firms who maintained unusually close relations with the extortion group, KrebsOnSecurity has learned. Sources close to the investigation say one of the executives in the United States even helped ShinyHunters operate a website that pressured victims into paying a ransom.

blog_news.title: Hackers breach Austrian Foreign Ministry website, access diplomats' contact details
blog_news.description: Austria's Foreign Ministry said late last week that hackers breached one of its websites and accessed the names and official contact information of employees at its Vienna headquarters and at Austria’s diplomatic missions abroad.

blog_news.title: Signal blocks screenshots by Apple, Google operating systems to protect data from AI agents
blog_news.description: Google’s Gemini Intelligence and Apple's Siri AI "are changing this environment in a way that’s making it increasingly hostile to privacy," Signal said.

blog_news.title: FBI reportedly facing second data breach involving National Crime Information Center
blog_news.description: The FBI is reportedly investigating a data breach involving the National Crime Information Center, a database used by U.S. law enforcement agencies that contains information on criminals, fugitives and missing people.

blog_news.title: CrowdStrike to purchase Zscaler for $43.9 billion
blog_news.description: “We see a path to become the largest AI safety and security company the world has ever seen,” CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz said.

blog_news.title: Norway says hackers exploited Microsoft security flaw to attack energy firms Equinor, Skagerak Energi
blog_news.description: Norwegian energy companies Equinor and Skagerak Energi were affected by a Microsoft cloud security vulnerability that hackers have exploited to target sensitive credentials, Norway's cybersecurity authorities said.

blog_news.title: Azure Flaw Exploited to Target Secrets at Norwegian Energy Firms
blog_news.description:
Microsoft closed an Azure API Management flaw exploited to target secrets at Norwegian energy companies, with other sectors also affected. 
 The post  Azure Flaw Exploited to Target Secrets at Norwegian Energy Firms  appeared first on  SecurityWeek .

blog_news.title: N-able Patches Critical Flaw Discovered After Mail Assure Cyberattack
blog_news.description:
The company has restored access to the affected services and continues to monitor the affected environments. 
 The post  N-able Patches Critical Flaw Discovered After Mail Assure Cyberattack   appeared first on  SecurityWeek .

blog_news.title: phpAfterShell Vulnerability Revives PHP2Shell’s Attack Path
blog_news.description:
If a session overwrite operation is interrupted, an attacker who controls the fresh data could trigger data deserialization and RCE. 
 The post  phpAfterShell Vulnerability Revives PHP2Shell’s Attack Path  appeared first on  SecurityWeek .

blog_news.title: GL.iNet Routers, KVMs Compromised via Remote Management Service Flaw
blog_news.description:
Attackers abused a flaw in the GoodCloud remote management service to push malware to devices, and cleaning them requires new firmware. 
 The post  GL.iNet Routers, KVMs Compromised via Remote Management Service Flaw  appeared first on  SecurityWeek .

blog_news.title: AI Inference Providers Failed to Detect Hacking and Prompt Theft, Says Dragos
blog_news.description:
Dragos uncovered undetected intrusions at three AI inference providers using nearly two million prompts sent to AI services. 
 The post  AI Inference Providers Failed to Detect Hacking and Prompt Theft, Says Dragos  appeared first on  SecurityWeek .

blog_news.title: BadBox 3.0 Ad Fraud Operation Generating 40 Billion Daily Bid Requests Disrupted
blog_news.description:
Backdoors on low-cost consumer devices served modules for ad fraud and for turning devices into residential proxies.  
 The post  BadBox 3.0 Ad Fraud Operation Generating 40 Billion Daily Bid Requests Disrupted  appeared first on  SecurityWeek .

blog_news.title: SAP NetWeaver, Cisco Expressway Flaws Exploited in Attacks
blog_news.description:
Threat actors could exploit them to leak or modify server information and to execute commands as root. 
 The post  SAP NetWeaver, Cisco Expressway Flaws Exploited in Attacks  appeared first on  SecurityWeek .

blog_news.title: CrowdStrike to Acquire Zscaler in $43.9 Billion Deal
blog_news.description:
CrowdStrike expects the combined company to have more than $10 billion in annual recurring revenue. 
 The post  CrowdStrike to Acquire Zscaler in $43.9 Billion Deal  appeared first on  SecurityWeek .

hibp_recent.name: Bromcom
hibp_recent.title: Bromcom
hibp_recent.description: In September 2026, UK education software provider Bromcom suffered a data breach involving a legacy single sign-on (SSO) registration system. The incident exposed 355k unique email addresses belonging to staff and pupils at UK schools, alongside SSO registration reference numbers. Bromcom confirmed that no passwords or authentication tokens were exposed, and that the incident did not enable access to Microsoft or Google accounts or its school management system.

hibp_recent.name: TooLost
hibp_recent.title: Too Lost
hibp_recent.description: In November 2026, an unauthorised party claimed to have obtained data from the music distributor for independent artists, Too Lost. The data contained 724k unique email addresses belonging to artists, their collaborators and fans. Some records also contained bcrypt password hashes, while a small subset included partial credit card data (last 4 digits and card type), identity verification information (in some cases, passport, driver's licence or national ID numbers), and payouts made to artists. Too Lost advised that its investigation remains ongoing, external forensic specialists have been engaged, and measures have been taken to secure affected systems and credentials. The company is also working with advisors to coordinate communications and support for affected individuals.

hibp_recent.name: Careers360
hibp_recent.title: Careers360
hibp_recent.description: In November 2026, data allegedly taken from the Indian education and careers platform Careers360 appeared on a public hacking forum. The 22M records included 3.6M unique email addresses alongside names, phone numbers, genders and caste categories, and most also contained students' entrance exam results, including ranks and marks.

hibp_recent.name: CastleRAT
hibp_recent.title: CastleRAT
hibp_recent.description: In November 2026, Europol and international law enforcement partners dismantled infrastructure supporting several malware operations. Among them was CastleRAT, a remote access trojan (RAT) that enabled criminals to remotely control infected computers. Europol provided HIBP with 180k email addresses associated with CastleRAT infections, along with 893k unique passwords observed more than 3M times across accounts used on infected computers. Later that month, Europol provided a further 251k unique email addresses and 1.3M passwords. The passwords from both datasets are now searchable via Pwned Passwords.

hibp_recent.name: YouHack
hibp_recent.title: YouHack
hibp_recent.description: In May 2013, the Russian-language hacking forum YouHack suffered a data breach that was later redistributed as part of a larger corpus of data. The breach exposed 107k forum members' email addresses, usernames, IP addresses and MD5 password hashes, most of which were unsalted. Forum posts also contained email address and password pairs belonging to other victims, bringing the total to 7.2M unique email addresses.

hibp_recent.name: SberSpasibo
hibp_recent.title: СберСпасибо (SberSpasibo)
hibp_recent.description: In March 2023, data allegedly taken from СберСпасибо (SberSpasibo), the loyalty program of Russian bank Сбербанк (Sberbank), was published online. The data contained records relating to 48M users, including 3.3M unique email addresses alongside phone numbers and dates of birth. Data also included bank card numbers stored as unsalted SHA-1 hashes, plus loyalty program details such as membership dates and the redemption of bonus points for partner offers.

hibp_recent.name: Harvard
hibp_recent.title: Harvard
hibp_recent.description: In November 2025, Harvard University suffered a data breach later linked to a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion attempt. The data contained 851k unique email addresses relating to the university's alumni and fundraising systems, along with extensive profile information for donors, alumni, parents and some faculty, staff and students. In Harvard's disclosure notice, the university stated that the breach impacted "personal information such as email addresses, telephone numbers, home and business addresses, event attendance, details of donations to the University, and other biographical information pertaining to University fundraising and alumni engagement activities".

hibp_recent.name: AfD
hibp_recent.title: AfD
hibp_recent.description: In September 2026, the German political party Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) suffered a data breach which exposed 345k unique email addresses. The following month, hundreds of gigabytes of data containing hundreds of thousands of emails and attachments was published online, with searchable AI-generated summaries and downloadable original files. An analysis of the incident reported that the breach was detected as early as 9 September, with a subsequent intrusion occurring five days later. In its public statement, AfD attributed the breach to an attack on a hosting provider, identified in subsequent reporting as the party-owned Alternita Dienstleistungs GmbH.

hibp_recent.name: AssuranceRetraite
hibp_recent.title: Assurance Retraite
hibp_recent.description: In September 2024, the French national pension fund Assurance Retraite suffered a data breach affecting approximately 370k assistance beneficiaries. The data included 70k unique email addresses along with names, dates of birth, physical addresses, phone numbers, income levels, marital statuses, French social security numbers (NIR) and contact details of relatives or other nominated contacts. In its disclosure notice, Assurance Retraite attributed the breach to a compromised partner account.

hibp_recent.name: GitesDeFrance
hibp_recent.title: Gîtes de France
hibp_recent.description: In May 2026, the French holiday rental network Gîtes de France suffered a data breach affecting some of its departmental branches. The incident exposed hundreds of thousands of customer records, including 118k unique email addresses alongside names, phone numbers, postal addresses and booking details.

hibp_recent.name: Crunchbase
hibp_recent.title: Crunchbase
hibp_recent.description: In January 2026, the private company intelligence platform Crunchbase was targeted in a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion attempt. Data allegedly obtained from the company was subsequently published publicly and included 560k unique email addresses, largely belonging to leads and business contacts. Other data included names, physical addresses, phone numbers, job titles, employers and LinkedIn profiles. Crunchbase later confirmed that a threat actor had exfiltrated documents from its corporate network.

hibp_recent.name: Sharecare
hibp_recent.title: Sharecare
hibp_recent.description: In August 2026, the digital health company Sharecare was the target of a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The group subsequently published data it claimed was taken from Sharecare's systems, containing 318k unique email addresses. Most of the data consisted of B2B sales and marketing records with names, physical addresses, phone numbers, job titles and employers. The data also included a small number of Brazilian health insurance plan members, including dates of birth, genders, marital statuses and CPF numbers (Brazilian taxpayer identification numbers).

hibp_recent.name: Neogen
hibp_recent.title: Neogen
hibp_recent.description: In August 2026, the food and animal safety organisation Neogen was the target of a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion attempt. The group later published data it claimed had been obtained from Neogen. The data consisted largely of corporate contact records and included 436k unique email addresses from mailing lists, employee records and other contacts.

hibp_recent.name: CyrusOne
hibp_recent.title: CyrusOne
hibp_recent.description: In August 2026, data centre operator CyrusOne was the target of a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion attempt. The group subsequently published data allegedly obtained from the company, which included 373k unique email addresses across records relating to users, sales leads and CyrusOne employees. The data largely consisted of corporate contact information, including names, physical addresses, phone numbers and job titles. It also included support tickets and other information related to the organisation's operations.

hibp_recent.name: DoubleCounter
hibp_recent.title: Double Counter
hibp_recent.description: In October 2026, the Discord server protection service Double Counter suffered a data breach attributed to a vulnerability in the Metabase analytics tool. In its disclosure notice, Double Counter advised that attackers gained access to a subset of its data. A corpus of data was subsequently published publicly and contained 275k unique email addresses and Discord usernames. A small number of records belonging to paying subscribers whose purchases were processed via Stripe were also present and included names, countries and postcodes.

hibp_recent.name: AngelOne
hibp_recent.title: Angel One
hibp_recent.description: In July 2024, the Indian stock brokerage firm Angel One confirmed that data leaked online related to a breach that occurred in April 2023. The leaked data included 7.9M user records containing 6.8M unique email addresses, along with names, physical addresses, phone numbers, bank account numbers, Permanent Account Numbers (PANs) and portfolio holdings. Angel One emphasised that the breach "has no impact on client securities, funds, or credentials".

hibp_recent.name: Medela
hibp_recent.title: Medela
hibp_recent.description: In September 2026, Swiss medical device company Medela was the target of a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The data allegedly obtained in the breach was later published publicly and included 424k unique email addresses belonging predominantly to healthcare professionals, Medela staff and leads. The exposed data consisted primarily of corporate contact information, including names, physical addresses and phone numbers, with some records also containing associated support tickets.

hibp_recent.name: LimeLeads
hibp_recent.title: LimeLeads
hibp_recent.description: In 2019, the now-defunct B2B marketing leads database service LimeLeads suffered a data breach due to an exposed, unsecured Elasticsearch server. The incident exposed tens of millions of records of largely corporate contact data containing 17.8M unique email addresses, along with phone numbers, employers, job titles and geographic locations including state, city and postcode.

hibp_recent.name: BurgerKingRussia
hibp_recent.title: Burger King Russia
hibp_recent.description: In October 2024, news of a data breach exposing Burger King Russia customers broke following an August attack on the Mindbox marketing automation platform. The breach exposed 3.2M unique email addresses along with names, genders, dates of birth, phone numbers and approximate geolocations, with the data spanning 2018 to August 2024. Burger King Russia acknowledged the incident and advised it did not include payment or passport details.

hibp_recent.name: Chess2026
hibp_recent.title: Chess.com (2026)
hibp_recent.description: In August 2026, millions of records allegedly sourced from Chess.com were posted online. The data contained 7.3M rows with 4.6M unique email addresses, along with usernames, names, countries and data relating to users' Chess.com accounts. Analysis of the data suggested it had been obtained by scraping. When loaded into HIBP, 99% of the email addresses had already appeared in previous data breaches, further supporting the scraping theory. Read more about scrapes and data breaches.

hibp_recent.name: McKesson
hibp_recent.title: McKesson
hibp_recent.description: In August 2026, healthcare and pharmaceutical company McKesson was targeted in a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The group subsequently published a substantial corpus of data they alleged was sourced from the company, which included 6.4M unique email addresses among other personal and corporate data attributes. The impacted data related to a range of individuals and roles, including marketing campaign recipients, patients, staff and healthcare provider contacts. In McKesson's disclosure notice, the company advised it had identified unauthorised access to "certain third-party applications and the exfiltration of certain data was associated with a subset of customers within our Oncology & Multispecialty and Medical-Surgical business units", but had "reasonable assurance of no ongoing unauthorized activity".

hibp_recent.name: ManchesterAirportsGroup
hibp_recent.title: Manchester Airports Group
hibp_recent.description: In August 2026, Manchester Airports Group (MAG) disclosed a data breach impacting their services. The incident was later claimed by the FulcrumSec hacking group, who subsequently published email addresses and phone numbers relating to 8.8M customers of Manchester, Stansted and East Midlands airports. The data contained personal information relating to airport services, including vehicle registrations and parking history, Fast Track purchases and lounge bookings. In their disclosure notice, MAG advised that "at no point has passenger safety or aviation security been compromised".

hibp_recent.name: Questel
hibp_recent.title: Questel
hibp_recent.description: In August 2026, the French intellectual property software and services company Questel was the target of a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The group subsequently published an extensive corpus of data they alleged was obtained from the company, largely comprising corporate contact information associated with sales leads, support cases and marketing activities, with 1.2M unique email addresses. The data also included names, employers and job titles, along with physical addresses and phone numbers.

hibp_recent.name: Carhartt
hibp_recent.title: Carhartt
hibp_recent.description: In August 2026, clothing retailer Carhartt was the target of a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The group subsequently published data allegedly obtained from the company including 12.9M unique email addresses, names, phone numbers and physical addresses. The published corpus also contained millions of synthetic records that did not relate to real individuals and were excluded from the breach.

hibp_recent.name: NIUS
hibp_recent.title: NIUS
hibp_recent.description: In July 2025, the German news service NIUS suffered a data breach which was subsequently leaked publicly. The data included 6k unique email addresses along with names, physical addresses and payment details for purchases including either IBANs or partial credit card data (masked card number, type and expiry).

hibp_recent.name: GolfCanada
hibp_recent.title: Golf Canada
hibp_recent.description: In mid-2026, hundreds of thousands of user records allegedly sourced from Golf Canada began circulating via Telegram. The data included 569k unique email addresses along with names, usernames, dates of birth, genders and approximate geographic locations (city, province and postcode). It remains unclear whether the data was obtained via unintentionally exposed website features or a security vulnerability.

hibp_recent.name: OzHairAndBeauty
hibp_recent.title: Oz Hair and Beauty
hibp_recent.description: In August 2026, Australian beauty retailer Oz Hair and Beauty was the target of an xpl0itrs extortion attack. The group subsequently published data allegedly obtained from the company, which included 2M unique email addresses along with names, phone numbers, geographic locations (suburb and postcode) and purchases.

hibp_recent.name: Fanlore
hibp_recent.title: Fanlore
hibp_recent.description: In August 2026, the Organization for Transformative Works (OTW) identified unauthorised access to the Fanlore wiki it operates. The breach resulted in the exposure of 145k unique email addresses along with usernames and passwords stored as either MD5 or PBKDF2 hashes. OTW self-submitted the exposed data to HIBP.

hibp_recent.name: RingCentral
hibp_recent.title: RingCentral
hibp_recent.description: In July 2026, the cloud-based business communications platform RingCentral was the target of a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The group subsequently published data they claimed was obtained from the platform, which included 1.6M unique email addresses along with names, physical addresses and phone numbers. In their disclosure notice, RingCentral advised that the incident affected "a limited portion of RingCentral customers" and that it was communicating directly with those affected.

hibp_recent.name: Alcon
hibp_recent.title: Alcon
hibp_recent.description: In August 2026, the Alcon eye care company was named in a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The group subsequently published data allegedly sourced from Alcon containing 218k unique email addresses along with other largely corporate B2B contact fields, including name, phone number and physical address.
